title: HINT for QA Engineers — cases derived, not imagined
metaDescription: Keep the SUT, requirements, negative paths and expected results together so assistants derive test cases and emit checkable Gherkin.
h1: Your assistant creates cases fast. HINT makes them follow the requirement.
intro: HINT keeps the system boundary, environment, coverage rules and expected results beside test artifacts. Your assistant derives cases from what is declared instead of filling a test plan with plausible paths.

situations.before: A generated suite covers only the successful login.
situations.body: Declared input boundaries and policy require meaningful failure and edge cases rather than a generic 'invalid input' row.

situations.before: Expected results describe what the current build happens to do.
situations.body: Each expected outcome traces to a requirement, so a defect cannot redefine the test to make itself pass.

situations.before: Steps assume an environment nobody prepared.
situations.body: The SUT version, fixtures and preconditions appear before the assistant writes or updates the case.

example.intro: The Nakatomi demo derives the main vault-login case from REQ-1.
example.after: It keeps the precondition and observable outcome tied to REQ-1, then the Gherkin emitter can reproduce the derivable scenario structure.
example.compiled:
<case name="TC-MAIN">
  Derived from REQ-1.
  <precondition name="Approved state">Declared setup.</precondition>
  <step name="Declared action">Perform it.</step>
</case>

never: Mark a case passed without an observed result.
Change an expected result to match faulty behavior.
Invent an environment, fixture or requirement boundary.
disclaimer: HINT defines and checks test knowledge; it does not execute your test suite or replace evidence from the system under test.

faq.a: No. It helps specify and verify the test artifacts; your existing runner executes them.

faq.q: Does the emitted Gherkin work with Cucumber?
faq.a: Yes. The Gherkin pack writes ordinary `.feature` structure; project-specific step implementations remain yours.
No. Expected results must come from declared requirements; otherwise the assistant reports a gap.

keywordDescriptions.plan: Sets the purpose, scope and exit conditions of a test effort.
keywordDescriptions.sut: Defines the system under test and its boundaries.
keywordDescriptions.case: Records a test case with a stable identifier.
keywordDescriptions.precondition: States setup that must be true before a case begins.
keywordDescriptions.expected: Names an observable result traced to a requirement.
keywordDescriptions.testdata: Constrains fixtures and values without inventing them.
keywordDescriptions.covers: Links a case to requirement or story identifiers.
keywordDescriptions.defect: Structures an observed mismatch without inventing results.
